name: zc_terminal_text_colour

tests.name: the terminal is open with its companion terminals on screen

detail.note: THE PRECONDITION. Every clause below reads pixels, and a shut terminal gives a beautifully consistent set of readings of the world behind it.

tests.name: the companion terminal reports where it is
the secondary colour is stored and read back as what was picked

detail.note: written through the same SaveAndApply the Colors tab's swatch calls, not a private path.

tests.name: picking the secondary colour changes the terminal's own pixels

detail.note: THE FOUNDER'S REQUEST, asked of the pixels. A setting that is stored and never drawn is the exact failure this project hit twice tonight -- a material property never applied, and a terminal whose chrome followed nothing at all.

tests.name: picking the SECONDARY left the accent alone

detail.note: half of independence. A secondary that drags the chrome with it has not been added, it has been aliased onto the primary.

tests.name: picking the PRIMARY afterwards left the words' colour alone

detail.note: THE OTHER HALF, and the one that catches a build where both are the same variable and only one of them was ever written to. Checked in both directions for that reason.

tests.name: the chrome still answers its own colour while the words keep theirs

detail.note: both hues present at once is what two independent colours look like. If the accent had swallowed the text, the green would collapse when the blue arrived.

tests.name: the founder's own terminal colours were put back
